args.subject: Bearing seat machining is the lab-supported explanation for the Q3 fixture widget recall
args.detail: Dossier: bearing seats may have been machined out of tolerance; lab report confirms seats 0.4 mm undersize on every recalled batch.

metrics.answerText:
## Q3 fixture widget recall — lab verdict

Read all three dossiers on the recall brief plus the independent lab report each one links. Exactly one is supported:

**✅ Supported: bearing seat machining**
- Dossier ([theory-bearing](http://127.0.0.1:40689/theory-bearing)): bearing seats may have been machined out of tolerance.
- Lab report ([lab-bearing](http://127.0.0.2:39333/lab-bearing)): "Bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined **0.4 mm undersize**. This theory is SUPPORTED."
- Rests on the measured bearing-seat diameter deviation of 0.4 mm undersize, consistent across every recalled batch.

**❌ Ruled out: ceramic coating cure**
- Dossier ([theory-coating](http://127.0.0.1:40689/theory-coating)): coat may have been cured too fast on the line.
- Lab report ([lab-coating](http://127.0.0.2:39333/lab-coating)): "Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported." — the measurement directly contradicts the too-fast cure premise.

**❌ Ruled out: packaging compression**
- Dossier ([theory-packaging](http://127.0.0.1:40689/theory-packaging)): widgets may have been compressed in transit by undersized packaging.
- Lab report ([lab-packaging](http://127.0.0.2:39333/lab-packaging)): "Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported." — packaging dimensions were on-spec, so transit compression is excluded.
